methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved dissecting sentences and code snippets into their core meanings and representing each as a distinct element in the sets X and Y.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Build an XOR gate using an assign statement (output out_assign).
Build an XOR gate using a combinational always block (output out_always_comb).
Build an XOR gate using a clocked always block (output out_always_ff).
The clocked always block produces a different circuit from the other two because the output is delayed.
Module has inputs clk, a, and b.
The clocked always block produces a different circuit if the output is assigned a value that depends on its previous value, thus inferring a flip-flop and creating a delayed output.
If the clocked always block implements purely combinational logic, it will behave similarly to the other two.
Synthesis tools might implement the clocked always block differently.
spec_atomic_units: The top module defines the interface of the design with inputs clk, a, b and outputs out_assign, out_always_comb.
The clk input and out_always_ff output are not relevant to the combinational logic specification and are therefore excluded in the pure combinational logic specification.
The combinational logic function implemented is the exclusive OR (XOR) operation.
XOR function: out = (a AND NOT b) OR (NOT a AND b).
Truth table represents XOR function.
out_assign and out_always_comb implement the XOR function.
out_assign output is generated using a continuous assignment statement: assign out_assign = a ^ b.
The assign statement continuously monitors the inputs a and b.
Whenever either input changes, the XOR operation is performed, and the result is immediately assigned to out_assign.
out_assign is implicitly a wire.
out_always_comb output is generated using a combinational always block: always_comb begin out_always_comb = a ^ b; end.
The always_comb block is a SystemVerilog construct specifically designed for describing combinational logic.
It implicitly creates a sensitivity list containing all input signals used within the block (in this case, a and b).
Whenever any of the signals in the implicit sensitivity list change, the block is executed, and the XOR operation is performed.
out_always_comb must be declared as a reg type.
Both the assign statement and the always_comb block implement the same XOR logic function.
out_assign and out_always_comb will have identical values at any given time, assuming no other processes are driving these signals.
The module implements an XOR gate three ways: using an assign statement (out_assign), a combinational always block (out_always_comb), and a clocked always_ff block (out_always_ff).
The assign and combinational always block outputs respond immediately to changes in inputs a and b.
The clocked always_ff block output is delayed by one clock cycle because it is updated only on the rising edge of the clock clk.
The module has three outputs: out_assign, out_always_comb, and out_always_ff.
out_assign changes continuously based on a and b.
out_always_comb changes whenever a or b changes.
out_always_ff changes only at the rising edge of clk, reflecting the values of a and b at that moment.
The critical path for out_assign and out_always_comb is the propagation delay through the XOR gate.
The critical path for out_always_ff is the clock-to-Q delay of the flip-flop, plus the setup time of the flip-flop relative to a and b changing before the rising edge of clk.
The module contains one register, out_always_ff.
It is updated on the positive edge of the clock clk.
The assignment out_always_ff <= a ^ b; is a non-blocking assignment.
out_always_comb is also declared as a reg, but it is assigned in a combinational always block, so it does not represent a register.
The assign statement for out_assign represents combinational logic.
